incident-bot: P1 ALERT 4423456789 — 2026-03-20T11:04:49Z — PeregrineAI (enterprise VPC) dedicated pool 'peregrine-dedicated' experiencing elevated 5xxs and repeated model reloads. Paging oncall rotation. Please ack in #incidents.
Amelia Chen: ACK. joining the thread. tagging @Devon and @Evan. I'll grab high-level metrics and customer contacts.
Devon Patel: looking now. gpu-host-17 shows repeated GPU OOMs and host-level restarts. Pod churn concentrated on tenant peregrine-42. CPU fine but GPU memory thrash leading to evictions.
Evan Li: runtime traces pulled. I see model load failures with a sequence of failed validations for model m-redwood/horizon-70b@v1.2. Rapid retries from loader triggered cache evictions: KV cache churn x8. Dumping runtime snapshot to /var/logs/peregrine/reload-dump-4423.tgz
Amelia Chen: any quick mitigations we can apply to stop the reload amplification? Prefer not to take the pool fully offline.
Devon Patel: we can put tenant into a soft-shed and route new requests to a standby shared pool. Command:
```
redwoodctl tenant modify --tenant peregrine --action soft-shed --target shared-standby-3 --note "stop reload loop"
```
Ops-Bot: request accepted. tenant peregrine set to soft-shed mode; traffic will be redirected within ~12s.
Priya Nair: pinging CSM and security SPOC for PeregrineAI. Also preparing short customer-facing update. Jordan, can you craft an internal exec blurb for the CTO? keep it tight.
Jordan Reyes: draft: "We've observed a model bundle validation failure causing reload storms on your dedicated pool. We've redirected traffic to reserve capacity and are replacing the affected host. We'll follow up with an RCA and remediation plan."
Evan Li: logs show bundle signature mismatch immediately followed by an automated fallback that attempted to fetch a different variant causing a loop:
```
[2026-03-20T11:03:12Z] model-loader ERROR bundle signature invalid for m-redwood/horizon-70b@v1.2
[2026-03-20T11:03:12Z] runtime INFO attempting fallback to latest-compatible
[2026-03-20T11:03:13Z] model-loader ERROR fallback bundle mismatch, triggering reload
```
Devon Patel: cordoned gpu-host-17 and draining pods. spun up instances in shared-standby-3 and starting workload migration. marking host for hardware inspection/firmware check.
Amelia Chen: agree with migration + pin to a known-good variant. Evan, can you initiate migration and pin model to v1.0-stable while we investigate bundle signing flow?
Evan Li: initiating migration:
```
redwoodctl migration run --tenant peregrine --src peregrine-dedicated --dst shared-standby-3 --pin-model m-redwood/horizon-70b@v1.0-stable --wait
```
Ops-Bot: migration initiated (job=66721). Progress updates every 30s.
Devon Patel: monitoring. GPU memory pressure easing on dedicated pool as pods drain. Other tenants unaffected so far.
Priya Nair: PeregrineAI CSM replied — they reported customer-side 502s and are preparing an emergency customer bridge. They asked if we can provide a preliminary estimate for credits. I'll coordinate bridge timing.
Jordan Reyes: suggest initial credit proposal of 12% for impacted window and offer a complimentary migration review. Will refine after we have exact request counts.
Amelia Chen: preliminary impact window based on error spike: 11:03:08 - 11:28:55 UTC. Estimated impacted requests ~3.6k. Peak error rate ~24%.
Evan Li: migration completed. KV cache hit ratio returning to baseline. Removing soft-shed in staged fashion but keeping reload-protection rules:
```
redwoodctl protection set --tenant peregrine --reloads max=3 interval=60s action=reject --note "prevent reload storms"
```
Ops-Bot: protection policy applied for tenant peregrine.
Devon Patel: host replacement underway for gpu-host-17. Created infra ticket INF-7300: "GPU host firmware/thermals investigation" assigned to infra with ETA 1 week for root-cause analysis.
Evan Li: runtime follow-ups: opened RNT-420: "Bundle signature preflight check & atomic swap" — ensure model bundle passes signature + checksum verification before activation in dedicated pools. Also RNT-421: "Graceful fallback gating" to avoid immediate fallback-triggered reload loops.
Amelia Chen: operational actions: create a policy to require 24h successful canary in shared pools before auto-promoting new model variants to dedicated pools. Also add a quick rollback playbook for tenants pinned to failing variants.
Devon Patel: created INT-7001: "Dedicated pool canary gating" for deployment team. ETA 3 weeks to implement enforcement through control plane.
Priya Nair: customer comm draft for bridge:
"Hi Peregrine team — we observed a model validation issue that caused repeated reloads on your dedicated pool leading to elevated 5xx responses between 11:0311:28 UTC. We redirected traffic to reserve capacity, replaced the affected host, and have applied protections to block reload storms. We're preparing a detailed RCA and will propose credits. Meeting invites sent."
Jordan Reyes: Peregrine CTO asked for assurance that their dedicated pool will not accept auto-deployed model variants until we add canary checks. We should confirm policy timeline and offer an interim manual gating option.
Amelia Chen: agreed. we'll offer manual gating for Peregrine until INT-7001 is in place. Devon, Evan — please co-author the RCA. I'll own the postmortem and timelines. Jordan/Priya — lead customer comms and credit negotiation.
Maria Alvarez: I'll coordinate with finance for fast-track credit approval if Peregrine requests it after the bridge. Also lining up compliance review for bundle signing pipeline.
Devon Patel: quick infra notes:
- ensure auto-evict playbooks have a faster cold-start path to avoid multi-minute capacity gaps
- improve host telemetry to surface pre-oom GPU mem spikes
Evan Li: runtime notes:
- add pre-activation bundle validation and atomic swap to prevent partial loads
- throttle retry logic in loader to exponential backoff with cap
- add per-tenant reload spike alerting in Console with runbook links
Jordan Reyes: scheduling internal postmortem review in 48h and will prepare an executive slide. Incident owners: Amelia Chen (lead), Devon Patel (infra), Evan Li (runtime). Priya Nair and Maria Alvarez on customer/credit comms.
Amelia Chen: final internal note: publish an internal incident timeline and artifacts in 48h. postmortem meeting set. tagging @incident-bot for reminders.
incident-bot: Reminder created: Postmortem due in 48h for incident 4423456789. Review meeting scheduled: 2026-03-22T11:00:00Z. Owners: Amelia Chen, Devon Patel, Evan Li, Jordan Reyes, Priya Nair.
Devon Patel: monitoring metrics for next 4h. will escalate on any regression. thanks team. :raised_hands:
Priya Nair: Peregrine bridge confirmed at 11:45 UTC. will post notes after call. Jordan — thanks for the drafts. :thumbsup:
